subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Jacobs <ethan.jacobs@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated - quick recap and next steps

Hi Ethan / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned. High-level notes from our discovery:

- Primary product: patient triage assistant embedded in Acme web/mobile app.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end for user-facing requests ~<200ms (you mentioned ~150-200ms target).
- Typical prompt size: ~120 tokens; some long-form prompts up to 600 tokens for batch jobs.
- Throughput: avg ~1,000 reqs/min with spikes to ~5,000 reqs/min during peak times (morning surge).
- Data / compliance: must support HIPAA controls, audit logs, and dedicated key management (we flagged Private as a possibility).

Initial recommendation from our side: given the combination of strict p95 latency targets and large bursty throughput, Dedicated capacity is the most predictable path to meet SLOs while avoiding noisy-neighbor variability. Hosted API can work for proofs-of-concept (and we can tune caching + batching) but may struggle to guarantee p95 at peak bursts without dedicated pool sizing.

Proposed next steps:
1) I can get Rishi to size a Dedicated pool for a 2-week POC that mirrors your traffic profile (we'll need sample traffic logs and 1-2 representative prompts).
2) Start the security questionnaire (I'll attach the QA doc) and surface any HIPAA-specific KMS/HSM questions to our security team.
3) Pricing & procurement: I'll send a scoped POC quote + terms. If POC meets SLOs we'll convert to a committed Dedicated contract (monthly/annual).

I've attached our deployment options PDF for reference. Are you available for a 30-min follow-up on Mon 6/15 to confirm traffic samples and kickoff sizing?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - quick recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. Couple clarifications:

- The 150-200ms p95 is our user-facing SLO (for the triage fast path). For async batch jobs (nightly summaries) we don't have strict latency.
- Throughput numbers look right: avg ~1k/min, peaks up to ~5k/min for a 10-20 minute window.
- We prefer dedicated capacity if that gives deterministic p95, but there's also interest in Private/VPC for HIPAA; however we need to see cost delta.

We'll prepare 48 hours of traffic logs and 2 representative prompts (one short, one long). Also, can you share a ballpark monthly cost for Dedicated vs Hosted (we're trying to evaluate commercial feasibility before procurement)?

Available for Mon 6/15 10:00am PT for the follow-up.

—Ethan

ethan.jacobs@acmehealth.com

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - quick recap and next steps

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Ethan.

Rishi, looping you in to size the Dedicated POC based on the sample logs. David, heads-up on potential HIPAA/private interest (cc'ing David Kim for security/compliance touchpoint).

High-level pricing guidance (ballpark) to help Acme decide quickly:
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): low commitment, higher per-token/unit cost; can be economical at low average traffic but may require fallback strategies during sustained peaks.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): higher base monthly cost but predictable unit economics and consistent p95 latency; recommended when p95 guarantees and throughput predictability matter.
- Private/VPC: adds infra & compliance overhead — reasonable if you require customer-managed network and strict audit/KMS requirements.

I'll assemble a scoped POC quote for Dedicated (2-week trial) and include both Dedicated and Hosted comparative pricing. For the POC sizing we'll need:
- 48 hours of request logs (timestamps, request size in tokens, latency where available)
- Typical prompt token distribution (short vs long)
- Any limits on burst concurrency you expect from the client side (e.g. connection pools, per-client rate limits)

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-estimate.xlsx (stub)

See you Mon 6/15 10:00am PT.

Best,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Jacobs <ethan.jacobs@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - quick recap and next steps

Thanks for the context — I pulled a quick estimate while we wait for logs. A few notes:

- Based on 1k avg / 5k peak with ~120 token median and p95 target <200ms, we're likely looking at a Dedicated pool sized roughly equivalent to 4x A100-class nodes (or 2-4x H100 depending on model choice and quantization). Exact sizing depends heavily on: model family, quantization, KV cache hotness, and whether you enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- If you can route user-facing low-latency traffic to a smaller trimmed model and batch non-real-time requests separately, we can reduce Dedicated footprint.
- For the POC we'll set up a canary route + load test to validate p95 across several burst patterns.

Action items for Acme:
1) Share 48h logs + sample prompts (secure upload link is fine).
2) Confirm which model families you want tested (we can start with an open LlamaX variant and test a higher-performing LLM if you prefer).

I'll prepare a short test plan and expected target metrics for the POC and attach a security QA doc for HIPAA items.

Attachment: security-qa.pdf (stub)

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
